source.title: LACoS-BLOOM: Low-rank Adaptation with Contrastive objective on 8 bits Siamese-BLOOM
source.authors: Wenhui Hua; Brian Williams; Davood Shamsi

record.tranche_reason: Tests the model-size trend in a new setting: fine-tuned BLOOM sentence-embedding models evaluated on downstream semantic-similarity tasks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream STS scores across BLOOM model sizes, including aggregate scores that rise with size. These bear on V6. It does not report held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling or fit a power law. Its adapter-selection validation losses, ablation comparisons, and cited results are not rows for the claim.
record.test_reason: Table 1 reports downstream STS scores for four BLOOM sizes (560m–7b1), each LoRA-fine-tuned the same way. This bears on V6's claim that downstream performance improves with scale, in a new setting (contrastive sentence-embedding fine-tuning). There is no fit, prediction or link to pretraining loss, so the evidence is a weak, descriptive scale trend.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say embedding quality is 'proportional' to parameters and unlabeled training data, and that 7b1 is best. Their evidence for the data claim is only a switch from SNLI+MNLI to multiNLI at 7b1, which changes the dataset, not just its amount. Their main conclusion is that LACoS-BLOOM gives efficient multilingual embeddings that beat SBERT and zero-shot BLOOM.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes quantized BLOOM models with LoRA and a contrastive objective, then measures downstream embedding-task scores. It does not measure held-out pretraining loss or fit scaling laws.
record.peer_reviewed: ReNeuIR’23: Workshop on Reaching Efficiency in Neural Information Retrieval
record.problems: The evidence is for downstream sentence-embedding scores rather than held-out pretraining loss. Only four BLOOM sizes are reported; no power-law fit, extrapolation test, uncertainty estimates, or compute-optimal allocation analysis is provided.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 also reports individual STS task scores, but the aggregate STS-Avg. and xSTS-Avg. rows capture the reported model-size trend. Table 2 compares zero-shot, LACoS-BLOOM and full-model fine-tuning at one model size, not a scaling trend.

untested.parts: Whether the improvement is predictable (no functional fit or extrapolation), and any relation to pretraining loss.
Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Power-law form in other regimes. Fine-tuning scores are reported, but no power law is fitted.
Dependence of exponents on fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a method paper; the scale result is incidental. Model sizes are confounded with per-size adapter-rank and learning-rate selection. There are no uncertainty estimates. The multiNLI rows (SBERT vs 7b1) compare methods, not scale, and correctly have no rows.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run held-out loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal allocation between parameters and tokens.
Effect of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law forms for held-out loss in other modalities or training regimes.
The study reports downstream scores by model size but does not fit a predictive relationship or test prediction from pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices.

rows.subject: LACoS-BLOOM-560m
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated downstream semantic-text-similarity performance across BLOOM model sizes.
rows.note: STS-Avg. is the reported average across STS12-16, STS-B and SICK-R.
rows.check: Each row is one point; the scale effect shows only across r1–r4. Adapter rank and hyperparameters were chosen separately per size (Fig. 4 grid search), which confounds size with tuning. The 560m model scores below the SBERT baseline (43.62 vs 58.42).

relationships.condition: English STS-Avg., LoRA+MNR fine-tuned BLOOM 560m–7b1 on SNLI+MNLI
relationships.reason: STS-Avg. rises monotonically with size: 43.62, 59.02, 60.50, 62.38 (r1–r4). Gains shrink sharply after 1b1, and there are only four points with no fit.
relationships.display_finding: STS-Avg. increased monotonically through 43.62, 59.02, 60.50, and 62.38, with sharply smaller gains after 1b1 and no predictive fit.

relationships.condition: Cross-lingual xSTS-Avg., same models, largest size step
relationships.reason: xSTS-Avg. rises from 560m to 3b1 (r5–r7) but is flat from 3b1 to 7b1 (56.75 vs 56.81, r7–r8). The gain from scale plateaus here.
relationships.display_finding: xSTS-Avg. improved from 560m to 3b1 but barely changed from 56.75 to 56.81 between 3b1 and 7b1.
